Updated read using Beige Book insights:
- Policy action: The FOMC raised the target range to 2.25–2.50% (IOER 2.40%) and maintained balance-sheet runoff and ON RRP operations, consistent with a still-constructive macro backdrop.
- Beige Book lens: District reports indicate continued job gains and tight labor markets with firms enhancing nonwage compensation (health benefits, profit-sharing, bonuses, paid vacation). Several districts (e.g., Dallas, Philadelphia, Kansas City, St. Louis) reported ongoing growth in economic activity. Household spending is supported by rising house prices in many markets. Price pressures remain uneven across districts, and falling fuel prices are easing headline inflation—consistent with inflation near, but not accelerating above, 2 percent.
- Credit/Investment context: SLOOS points to tighter standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and softer demand in rate-sensitive, investment-linked sectors, reinforcing the FOMC’s note that business fixed investment has moderated.
- Net: The Beige Book corroborates broad strength in labor markets and consumption but highlights mixed pricing pressures and bank-channel tightening. This tilts the stance from mildly hawkish toward balanced/cautious despite the rate hike and ongoing normalization.
